children: Dutch and British gas prices rose on Wednesday morning, tracking a rise in Asian liquefied natural gas prices, as concerns over tough competition for limited supply with low storage outweighed bearish fundamentals driven by rising Norwegian imports and lower gas demand from the power sector.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was up  €1.30 at €77.00  per megawatt hour or around $25.21/mmBtu, by 0820 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) was up 1.94 pence at 190.51 pence per therm.
“On top of the uncertainty coming from the Middle East, fundamentals are rather bearish," said LSEG analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich.

Total LNG sendout - the amount of gas flowing from LNG terminals into the Northwest European grid - is stable day-on-day. Meanwhile, Norwegian imports may increase as maintenance ends and gas for power demand is forecast to fall by 177 gigawatt hour per day on rising wind, offsetting a rise in gas for heating demand, which is 90GWh/d higher as temperatures cool, Dauhalevich said.
Europe’s gas storage sites are 72.83% full, Gas Infrastructure Europe data showed, well below historical levels for this time of the year.

“Flows from the Persian Gulf have picked up slightly in the last couple of weeks. However, risks were highlighted by reports that a Greek-owned LNG tanker was hit by an unidentified object while sailing near the Strait of Hormuz," said Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at ANZ.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract <> was down €0.15 at €84.63 a metric ton.
